subject: SunPeak procurement: PO field mapping, prepay/holdback & invoice release cadence
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@sunpeak.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@sunpeak.com
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Procurement: PO structure, net terms, and invoice release cadence

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo last week — excited about the fit. Procurement asked me to consolidate a few requirements so we can scope SOW and do a PO correctly: 

- Our ERP requires one PO number per legal entity + a project code on each invoice line (we have three entities that may be in scope).
- Invoices must reference the PO number and the internal project code in the header and in each line item.
- Standard SunPeak net terms are net90. We know vendors push back on net90; indicate if you can accept net45 or net30.
- For large annual contracts we normally hold back 10% as acceptance holdback, released at the completion of onboarding milestones.
- Invoice cadence: preferred monthly consolidated invoice submitted on the first business day of the month; can accept weekly consolidated statements for fast-moving usage accounts but ERP will only accept one invoice per PO per period.

We attached our PO template so your finance team can confirm field mapping and header format. Also include any standard language you need in the PO (billing address, remit-to, tax IDs).

Can you confirm: (1) whether Redwood can map to our PO fields and include project codes, (2) what net terms you can accept, and (3) how Redwood handles holdbacks and invoice consolidation for multi-entity clients?

Elena
SunPeak Procurement

Attachment: SunPeak_PO_Template.pdf (application/pdf)
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@sunpeak.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement: PO structure, net terms, and invoice release cadence

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list and the template. Looping in Vanessa and Karthik from enterprise sales to help with commercial levers. Quick answers up front:

1) PO mapping: yes — our billing pipeline can populate a PO number per legal entity and include a project code on each line item. We'll need a sample export from your ERP (field names) but the template you sent is a good start.

2) Net terms: Redwood's standard hosted-contract payment term is net30. For enterprise deals we can consider longer terms (net45 or net60) in exchange for either a commitment (monthly/annual committed spend) or an advance.

3) Holdback: we typically avoid multi-month holdbacks for hosted services. We can do a 5–10% acceptance holdback tied to clearly defined onboarding milestones; alternatively we can structure a smaller holdback and provide a set of onboarding credits and a dedicated onboarding manager to reduce perceived risk.

Next steps: Vanessa / Karthik — can you propose a commercial tradeoff (discount schedule vs term vs upfront) we can offer here? I'll attach a draft SOW and propose a short call with procurement to review PO mapping.

Thanks,
Mateo
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Draft_SOW_SunPeak_v3.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-21T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement: PO mapping & terms — quick commercial options

Mateo / Karthik — notes from my side with commercial levers we can use for SunPeak: 

- Option A (commit + best price): 12-month committed MRR, quarterly prepay (invoice at start of quarter), 10% list discount. No holdback. Redwood provides monthly usage reports and a one-week acceptance window per milestone.

- Option B (mid): 12-month commitment, no prepay, net45, 6% list discount, 5% onboarding holdback released after milestone sign-off. Redwood provides onboarding credit equal to first month invoice.

- Option C (conservative for finance): No long-term commitment, net60 or net90 with a 10% holdback and 3% discount only. (Low chance to be approved by our revenue ops team.)

I prefer Option B as a compromise — keeps SunPeak's cash flexibility while protecting Redwood. If they insist on net90 we can ask for a higher upfront (eg 30% deposit) to bridge.

Pricing note: discounts above are off list (not net of usage overages) and apply to committed baseline only; overages billed at standard rates.

Let me know if you want me to draft the commercial summary to send to procurement.

—Vanessa
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@sunpeak.com>
Cc: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-22T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood commercial proposal — PO mapping, invoice cadence & compromise on terms

Hi Elena — following up with a concise proposal that addresses the items you raised and gives a path to sign-off: 

Proposal (summary):
- PO & ERP mapping: Redwood will include the PO number and the SunPeak project code on each invoice line. We will validate the exact field names with a one-time integration checklist.
- Invoice cadence: Redwood will provide a single consolidated invoice per PO per month. In cases where you elect weekly statements, those will be consolidated and tied back to the monthly ledger for ERP reconciliation.
- Net terms & holdback: Redwood can accept net45 if SunPeak signs a 12-month commitment. As an alternative, we can accept net60 with a 20% upfront deposit.
- Holdback compromise: 5% holdback tied to onboarding milestones (detailed in attached SOW) OR waive holdback if SunPeak provides a 20% deposit at contract execution.
- Commercial discount: 6% discount off list for the committed baseline under net45 (Option B). 10% discount available under Option A (quarterly prepay).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether you prefer net45 + 6% discount (and 5% holdback) or net60 + 20% deposit (holdback waived).
2) If net45, we will send a DocuSign packet (SLA + PO instruction addendum) and the final SOW.

I can jump on a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk the procurement team through the PO field mapping if helpful.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Director — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Links: Draft SOW (https://drive.redwood.com/shared/SunPeak/Draft_SOW_SunPeak_v3) | DocuSign (https://app.docusign.com/envelope/12345-abcde)
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@sunpeak.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Jacob Stern <j.stern@sunpeak.com>, procurement@sunpeak.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-23T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood commercial proposal — PO mapping, invoice cadence & compromise on terms

Karthik — thanks, this framing helps. Procurement likes Option B but asks for one tweak: can Redwood accept net45 but reduce the upfront deposit from 20% to 10% if we extend the net45 payment window for the first two invoices to net60 as a transitional concession? This helps our cash ops while giving your team more comfort early.

Also need a short mapping doc we can hand to our ERP team: exact invoice XML field names or a CSV header mapping. Can your billing team produce that? If so, we'll route the draft PO (we will include three entity references) and target signature by end of next week.

We are good to proceed with the DocuSign packet once we have the mapping doc and the SOW updated with the 5% holdback milestone schedule.

Elena
SunPeak Procurement
